subject: Post-call: Hyperscaler delta & private networking test plan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Hyperscaler delta & private networking test plan

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment.

Key takeaways from our call:
- FinBank is running a competitive evaluation: Redwood inference vs hyperscaler-managed LLM endpoints. Primary concerns are predictable latency (tail), private/VPC-only deployment options, and air-gapped feasibility for regulated workloads.
- Your CloudOps team needs clarity on network topology, control-plane ownership, and how an air-gapped ingest/updates flow would work (signed artifacts / removable media).
- Success criteria for a POC: 95th-percentile latency < 150ms for 1k QPS synthetic workload (long-seq workload), zero egress to public internet during restricted tests, and KMS integration for key separation.

Proposed mutual test plan (attached: networking-test-matrix-v1.xlsx):
1) "No-egress" control-plane test — run with Redwood-managed control plane but block outbound egress from the workload subnet; verify 503 fallback behavior and local-only inference with pre-seeded models.
2) Private control-plane variant — demo customer-hosted control plane (VPC peering/Transit GW) and validate that all control plane RPCs route over private links.
3) Air-gap emulation — deploy model artifacts from an offline signed bundle, validate bootstrapping and HSM/KMS-less key handoff flow.
4) Head-to-head latency run — Redwood vs Hyperscaler A, same model family and CPU/GPU profile, capture cold-start and steady-state tail latencies.

Immediate asks from your side:
- Can CloudOps share the target subnet ranges and whether Direct Connect or Transit Gateways are required for private peering?
- Which KMS/HSM vendor do you want us to validate against (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or customer HSM)?

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi will follow up with a short note on networking specifics and the control-plane variants we can support.
- We'll schedule a 60-min lab kickoff with CloudOps to run the "no-egress" control-plane trial next week.
- I attached a short comparison doc (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-latency-delta.pdf) that highlights our typical cold-start mitigation strategies and batching/caching tradeoffs.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Scheduling after Rishi confirms availability.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-latency-delta.pdf, networking-test-matrix-v1.xlsx, airgap-criteria-checklist.md

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudOps Team <cloudops@finbank.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hyperscaler delta & private networking test plan

Naomi — appreciate the recap. A few clarifying items from our architecture side before we lock in dates:

1) For the "no-egress" control-plane test: are you able to run the runtime entirely without reaching the Redwood control plane (i.e., local-only with pre-warmed KV cache)? If not, what minimal control-plane RPCs are expected?

2) For the private control plane: we prefer customer-hosted control plane (we plan to route via our Transit GW). Can you confirm support for AWS Direct Connect and for peering with our Azure tenant (hybrid)?

3) Air-gap: our compliance team will require a signed artifact chain and an auditable checksum verification. Does Redwood provide a signed manifest and a deterministic model artifact hash?

4) KMS: priority is our Thales HSM for keys. Will you be able to show a PoC with Thales or do you require AWS KMS as intermediary?

We can target a lab kickoff on Tue 4/20 10:00am PT if that works for your team.

— Alex
Alex Chen | Head of Platform Security
FinBank (alex.chen@finbank.com)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finbank.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hyperscaler delta & private networking test plan

Alex — thanks for the excellent questions. Technical clarifications below (and I added a short checklist to the attached matrix).

1) No-egress control-plane test:
- We support a local-only runtime mode for the POC where model weights and KV cache are pre-seeded. In that mode, the runtime does not attempt outbound model fetching or telemetry uploads (we can disable telemetry).
- Minimal control-plane RPCs (if you choose Redwood-managed control plane) are for model rollforward checks and rollout heartbeat. For the blocked test we'll set rollforward=manual so no outbound calls are required.

2) Private control plane / peering:
- Redwood supports both AWS Direct Connect and Azure ExpressRoute via standard VPC/VNet peering patterns. Transit Gateway peering is supported — we'll supply a CloudFormation / ARM template for the peering setup.
- For hybrid (AWS <-> Azure) peering we recommend a brokered Transit GW approach; our network team has done this for a handful of regulated banks.

3) Air-gap artifact flow:
- We publish signed manifests (SHA-256) for model artifacts and provide a GPG-signed release bundle. The runtime verifies manifest signature and artifact checksums on boot. We can add extra attestation lines for your compliance team.

4) HSM / KMS:
- We currently have validated integrations with AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault. We have done custom integrations with Thales HSM for a partner — for a PoC we can bring a Thales engineer to the kickoff or run a mediated flow where keys are wrapped by your HSM and Redwood uses wrapped keys. Please confirm which path you prefer.

Lab kickoff: Tue 20 Apr 2027 10:00am PT works for us. I propose the following agenda (60m):
- 0-10m: introductions & goals
- 10-25m: network topology review and peering checklist (collect subnets / routing)
- 25-40m: run "no-egress" local-only boot with seeded model (observability hooks enabled)
- 40-55m: verify manifest signature & checksum, run small latency run vs Hyperscaler A baseline
- 55-60m: next steps & schedule extended performance run

I'll bring a short script to capture packet flows (MTU, path MTU, and any NAT behavior) so we can validate there are no accidental egress paths.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Infrastructure & Integrations
Redwood Inference
